data.name: ProcessObservation.Report.Boundary
data.value: One selected process instance is observed, not the whole application or its child processes. PID is checked together with creation time; after exit, observation does not switch to a new process. CPU is the share of total system processor time, accounting for the number of active logical processors; it is not the share of the process affinity or quota. Working set includes shared resident pages; private commit is committed private memory, not physical RAM occupied. I/O is Windows-accounted process I/O bytes, not physical disk speed. The first sample and gaps do not produce rates. Process and computer are read sequentially with separate timestamps on one monotonic timeline; there is no atomic snapshot. Coincidence between load and a symptom does not establish cause. Measurements and the collector may affect load; no artificial load or remediation is started.
